LSE 0.5.7 decodes code at **157.7 tok/s with DFlash2** on an R9700 under macOS: a HumanEval-style prompt, 640 tokens out, temperature 0.6, 98.4% draft acceptance. On the same GPU under Linux, the packaged archive decodes the same prompt at 126.5 tok/s. A Radeon 8060S (gfx1151) decodes it at 55.5 tok/s.

DFlash2 and MTP now choose how many draft tokens to verify at each step. The choice comes from the draft's confidence and the cost of each width measured on the GPU. Both are on by default.

**Requires mac_linuxgpu v0.1.151 (build 255) or later** on macOS. Kernel arguments in VRAM need **v0.1.161 (build 265)**. The macOS measurements below were taken on v0.1.162 (build 266).

## Changes

1. **Adaptive verify width for DFlash2 and MTP, on by default.**
   - For each sampled step, DFlash2 verifies the prefix of its seven proposals that is expected to decode fastest on this GPU. MTP chains up to seven proposals.
   - `--adaptive-dflash2=off` and `--adaptive-mtp=off` keep the fixed widths. In libLSE these are `lse_config.adaptive_dflash2` and `adaptive_mtp`.
   - A request that sets `mtp_depth` keeps that depth.
   - Greedy (temperature 0) requests always verify the fixed width, so greedy output does not change.
   - Measured against the fixed widths on the R9700 (temperature 0.6, median of 36 runs each):

     | Prompt | DFlash2, adaptive vs fixed | MTP, adaptive vs `--mtp-depth 3` |
     | --- | ---: | ---: |
     | Code | -0.3% | +27.7% |
     | 2K prompt | +0.4% | -1.8% |
     | 4K prompt | +2.7% | -2.4% |
     | Essay | +8.8% | -5.3% |

   - Adaptive MTP is slower than a fixed depth of 3 on prose and long prompts. `--adaptive-mtp=off` restores depth 3.
2. **Verify passes of every width run on the four- or eight-row kernels.** A verify width with no kernel of its own previously fell back to slower contractions. On gfx1201, 2 and 3 rows now run on the four-row kernels and 5 to 7 rows on the eight-row ones, with the extra rows masked. DFlash2 verify pass on the R9700, ms per pass at 1 to 8 rows:
   - before: 31.4, 35.2, 48.8, 33.0, 74.9, 51.5, 89.2, 37.6
   - after: 31.4, 32.3, 32.7, 33.0, 33.7, 35.2, 36.0, 37.7

   This is what lets adaptive DFlash2 choose any width.
3. **Faster warm starts.**
   - The kernel cache keeps a launch index beside the compiled kernels. A warm start makes every prepared kernel resident without generating its source.
   - Loading the pinned DFlash2 configuration with the kernel cache on disk takes 4.9 s on the Mac.
   - A cache entry that fails its checksum is reported, removed and rebuilt from source.
4. **Perplexity and KL divergence.**
   - `lse-server --perplexity FILE` scores a text through the same prefill kernels, attention and KV dtype that serving uses. It follows llama.cpp's chunk method by default; `--perplexity-method sliding` uses sliding windows instead.
   - `--perplexity-kld-base-out` and `--perplexity-kld` record and compare a top-k KL-divergence base.
   - See `docs/PERPLEXITY.md` and the quality results below.
5. **Kernel variants measured on the device.**
   - A kernel can offer several layouts of the same computation. The first time it runs, every variant runs on real operands. Any variant whose output differs from variant 0 in a single byte is refused.
   - The fastest variant is kept only if it beats variant 0 by more than 2%.
   - Decisions are cached in `variants-<release>.txt` in the kernel cache. `LSE_AUTOTUNE=off` runs variant 0 everywhere.
6. **RDNA3.5 (gfx1151):**
   - Whole-fragment WMMA operand loads in the prefill GEMM: the Q4 GEMM runs at 31 TFLOPS instead of 18.
   - FlashPrefill V2 is on by default.
   - MTP's four-row verify passes run in one row group with a fused SwiGLU.
   - The odd verify widths run on the four- and eight-row kernels.
   - The eight-row attention projections compute two columns per wave.
   - The eight-row SwiGLU panel is staged in scratch.
   - The 8-bit draft's matrix panel uses per-shape K splits.
   - gfx1201's generated kernels are byte-identical across this work.
7. **Linux:** loomc's compile-memory accounting now subtracts frees.

Greedy (temperature 0) output on the pinned configuration is byte-identical to 0.5.6. This was checked on the Mac with DFlash2 (256- and 512-token prompts) and plain decoding (256-token prompt).

## Performance on macOS (R9700)

Qwen3.8-27B Q4 with the Q8 DFlash2 draft on an R9700 over Thunderbolt 5, Apple M5 Max, mac_linuxgpu v0.1.162 (build 266), LSE 0.5.7 macOS package.
- Server flags: `--batch-size 1024 --ubatch-size 1024 --kv-cache-dtype bf16 --kv-len 262100 --temperature 0.6`, with `LSE_REQUIRE_DEVICE_KERNELS=1`.
- Adaptive verify width is on (the default).
- Each mode runs in one server session. Timing starts after about 1.5 s of sustained decode.

**Decode, temperature 0.6.** Draft acceptance is in parentheses.

| Prompt | DFlash2 | MTP=3 | Plain |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Code**: HumanEval-style, six functions to implement (302 prompt tokens, 640 out) | **157.7 tok/s** (98.4%) | 115.6 tok/s (97.2%) | 32.0 tok/s |
| 2K prompt (2,406 tokens, 256 out) | 70.4 tok/s (74.6%) | 54.4 tok/s (69.8%) | 31.6 tok/s |
| 4K prompt (4,786 tokens, 256 out) | 66.5 tok/s (75.1%) | 55.6 tok/s (73.6%) | 31.1 tok/s |
| Essay (32 prompt tokens, 640 out) | 66.4 tok/s (70.2%) | 61.3 tok/s (70.1%) | 32.3 tok/s |

Run counts:
- DFlash2 (every prompt) and MTP=3 code: median of five runs.
- MTP=3's other prompts and plain: median of three runs.

Mean verify width, in rows per pass (maximum 8):
- DFlash2: 7.9 on code, 5.7 at 2K, 5.6 at 4K, 5.7 on the essay.
- MTP=3: 6.9 on code, 4.8 at 2K and 4K, 5.0 on the essay.

**Time to first token** over the HTTP API, DFlash2 server, 128 tokens out:
- Cold is the first request of that size after the server starts, with the kernel cache on disk.
- Warm is the median of three requests after a warm-up.

| Prompt tokens | Warm TTFT | Warm prefill | Cold TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 137 | 0.122 s | 1,127 tok/s | 0.182 s |
| 271 | 0.201 s | 1,345 tok/s | 0.199 s |
| 532 | 0.373 s | 1,425 tok/s | 0.375 s |
| 646 | 0.436 s | 1,483 tok/s | 0.434 s |
| 1,060 | 0.663 s | 1,599 tok/s | 0.672 s |
| 2,118 | 1.292 s | 1,640 tok/s | 1.289 s |
| 4,230 | 2.589 s | 1,634 tok/s | 2.596 s |
| 33,799 | 23.91 s | 1,414 tok/s | 24.09 s |

**Model load**, launch to ready with the checkpoint in the file cache and the kernel cache on disk:
- 4.9 s with DFlash2, 3.4 s with MTP, 3.8 s plain.
- Host memory footprint at ready with DFlash2: 422 MB.
- The first launch of a new LSE build compiles every request shape's kernels before it reports ready. With an empty kernel cache this took 110.8 s with DFlash2.

MS-S1 MAX with a Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), ROCm 7.13, Ubuntu 24.04, pinned Qwen3.8-27B Q4 configuration, built from the release source (`4a2e2fa`, before the version bump), adaptive verify width on. Medians of three runs after a warm-up, temperature 0.6, with draft acceptance in parentheses:

| Prompt | DFlash2 | MTP=3 | Plain |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Code** (HumanEval-style, 640 out) | **55.5 tok/s** (99.1%) | 34.9 tok/s (96.9%) | 13.6 tok/s |
| 2K prompt (256 out) | 23.2 tok/s (75.2%) | 20.8 tok/s (70.1%) | 13.5 tok/s |
| 4K prompt (256 out) | 24.3 tok/s (77.9%) | 23.6 tok/s (83.3%) | 13.3 tok/s |
| Essay (640 out) | 25.3 tok/s (72.0%) | 20.5 tok/s (65.4%) | 13.7 tok/s |

Mean verify width:
- DFlash2: 8.0 on code, 5.3 at 2K, 5.5 at 4K, 4.9 on the essay.
- MTP=3: 6.3 on code, 3.9 at 2K, 4.0 at 4K and on the essay.

Prefill with the DFlash2 server, FlashPrefill V2 on:

| Prompt | TTFT | Prefill |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 256 | 0.636 s | 403 tok/s |
| 512 | 1.205 s | 425 tok/s |
| 1K | 2.020 s | 507 tok/s |
| 2K | 4.111 s | 498 tok/s |
| 4K | 8.364 s | 490 tok/s |
| 32K | 47.73 s | 687 tok/s |

Load:
- With the kernel cache on disk: 4.6 s plain, 6.1 s with MTP.
- First launch with an empty kernel cache: 110.9 s plain. DFlash2's first start compiled its own kernels in 116.3 s.

## Linux (R9700, ROCm 7.13)

The packaged `lse-v0.5.7-linux-x86_64` archive, run from an extracted copy on an R9700 (ROCm 7.13, Ubuntu, built with GCC 16.0.1 and CMake 4.2.3). Pinned Qwen3.8-27B Q4 configuration, default dialect (Loom), `LSE_REQUIRE_DEVICE_KERNELS=1`, adaptive verify width on, temperature 0.6. Draft acceptance is in parentheses.

| Prompt | DFlash2 | MTP=3 | Plain |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Code** (HumanEval-style, 640 out) | **126.5 tok/s** (98.4%) | 95.2 tok/s (96.7%) | 26.3 tok/s |
| Essay (640 out) | 46.9 tok/s (68.9%) | 45.4 tok/s (68.9%) | 26.8 tok/s |

- Each cell is the median of eight runs over two server sessions.
- The host is a shared server. Its CPU load average was 15 to 23 during these runs, and individual runs varied widely: DFlash2 code ranged from 110.3 to 133.3 tok/s.
- Load with the kernel cache on disk: 19.9 s with DFlash2, 9.9 s with MTP, 11.0 s plain. A first launch with no kernels in the cache takes 299 s with DFlash2.

**Runtime requirements**, read from the binaries' symbol versions:
- glibc 2.43 or later.
- The GCC 16 libstdc++ (`GLIBCXX_3.4.35`).
- ROCm 7.x `libamd_comgr.so.3` and `libhsa-runtime64.so.1`.

That is an Ubuntu 26.04-class system. The archive bundles HRX and the patched Loom compiler.

**Optional kernel patch for RDNA4.**
- Linux users with GFX12 (RDNA4) cards, such as the R9700 or RX 9070, can apply ["drm/amdkfd: Put GFX12 compute queue MQDs in VRAM"](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/mac_linuxgpu/blob/main/patches/linux/kfd-v12-mqd-vram.patch) to the amdgpu driver.
- What it changes:
  - KFD compute-queue descriptors (MQDs) are allocated in CPU-visible VRAM instead of system memory.
  - HDP is flushed at the end of `update_mqd`.
  - Upstream already does both for GFX 9.4.3.
- What was measured: the stall on a dispatch that exactly fills a shader engine (for example 253 to 256 workgroups of 256 threads).
  - On the Mac driver, which runs the same amdgpu code, it dropped from 51 µs to 17 µs.
  - Stock Linux measured 26 µs on the same dispatch.
- It has not been measured on a patched Linux kernel.
- It applies to GFX12 only. Graphics and Vulkan are unaffected.

## Output quality

Wikitext-2 perplexity, Qwen3.8-27B, llama.cpp's method: 512-token chunks, 580 chunks, the second half of each chunk scored, 147,900 tokens scored. Both engines see the same 297,193 token ids.

| Engine | Weights | Perplexity |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| LSE 0.5.7 (`lse-server --perplexity`) | MLX 4-bit affine, group 64 (`qwen38-27b-q4-mlx`) | 7.1467 ± 0.0464 |
| llama.cpp b11379, Vulkan (RADV), `llama-perplexity` | GGUF Q4_0 (unsloth `Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_0.gguf`) | 7.0759 ± 0.0461 |

- The two use different 4-bit quantizations of the same model. The 0.0708 gap comes from the checkpoints and the implementations together.
- LSE's value is identical on the R9700 under macOS and Linux, and on gfx1151 (7.146670).
- At 512-token chunks, FlashPrefill V2 and dense attention score the same.
- With 2,048-token sliding windows: FlashPrefill V2 7.0487, dense 7.0368 (+0.0119).

## Tests

- **macOS host suite:** 61 of 61 and 4 of 4 pass.
- **GPU tests on the R9700 (macOS, release build):**
  - Passing in full: `test_runtime` 95 of 95, `test_q4_gemm` 4 of 4, `test_quant_prefill` 8 of 8.
  - `test_graph`: 124 of 127. The three failing cases are the same as in 0.5.6.
  - `test_dflash2`: 25 of 37. The same cases fail as in 0.5.6.
- **Linux (ctest on the R9700):** 101 of 104 pass. The three failures:
  - `test_graph`: the same three cases as on macOS.
  - `test_jit`: `a_traffic_model_that_forgets_a_term_disagrees_with_the_object`, as in 0.5.6.
  - `test_quant_operand_cache` (new in 0.5.7): "unsupported M3 row capacity changed legacy plan". It fails only in the legacy HIP dialect's emitter, where a three-row contraction now takes the four-row plan. The Loom emitter passes the same case, and Loom is the default dialect.
- **Smoke test:** the Linux smoke script passes all checks. On macOS, the packaged `lse` CLI and `lse-server` ran on the R9700 with `LSE_REQUIRE_DEVICE_KERNELS=1`.

## Downloads

| Asset | For |
| --- | --- |
| `lse-v0.5.7-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | macOS 15+ on Apple Silicon with an external AMD GPU and the [mac_linuxgpu](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/mac_linuxgpu) driver |
| `lse-v0.5.7-ios-arm64.xcframework.zip` | iOS/iPadOS 26+ apps that embed the mac_linuxgpu driver. Contains `LSE.xcframework`, built with the mac_linuxgpu v0.1.162 (build 266) HSA runtime |
| `lse-v0.5.7-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | Linux x86_64 with ROCm 7.x, glibc 2.43+ and the GCC 16 libstdc++ (an Ubuntu 26.04-class system). Targets `gfx942`, `gfx1150`, `gfx1151`, `gfx1200`, `gfx1201` |

Each asset has a `.sha256` beside it.

libLSE changes:
- `lse_config` gains two `int32_t` fields at its end, `adaptive_dflash2` and `adaptive_mtp`. Both are on after `lse_config_init`.
- A new function, `lse_perplexity`, scores a text.
- `LSE_ABI_VERSION` is still 1. Rebuild apps against the 0.5.7 header and keep calling `lse_config_init` before setting fields.
